The best definition of ecological efficiency is the ratio between energy flows at different points in a food chain.

Ecological efficiency refers to the efficiency with which energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next in an ecosystem.

It is typically expressed as a percentage and is calculated by comparing the amount of energy available at one trophic level to the amount of energy that is transferred to the next trophic level.

This concept helps ecologists understand the flow of energy through ecosystems and the limitations on the number of trophic levels that can be supported.

· The Wainganga River is NOT a Himalayan river.

· It is a major peninsular river that originates in the Satpura Range in Madhya Pradesh, Central India, and flows south to join the Godavari River system.

· Himalayan rivers originate from the glaciers and ranges of the Himalayas.

Explanation of Other Options:

· Beas River: This river originates in the Himalayas in central Himachal Pradesh, India, specifically from the Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass. It is a tributary of the Sutlej River (Indus system).

· Ravi River: This river also originates in the Himalayas, in the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh, India. It is one of the five rivers of Punjab and a tributary of the Indus.

· Teesta River: This river originates from the Pauhunri (or Teesta Kangse) glacier in the Himalayas in Sikkim, India. It flows through Sikkim and West Bengal before entering Bangladesh, where it joins the Brahmaputra River (Jamuna).

Further insights:

· Indian rivers are broadly classified into Himalayan rivers (perennial, fed by glaciers and rain) and Peninsular rivers (mostly seasonal, rain-fed, though some larger ones are perennial).

· The Wainganga is part of the Godavari basin, which is the largest peninsular river system in India.

Total internal reflection occurs when light passes from a denser medium to a rarer medium.

When light travels from a denser medium (like water or glass) to a rarer medium (like air), it bends away from the normal (the line perpendicular to the surface). As the angle of incidence increases, the angle of refraction also increases.

At a certain angle (the critical angle), the angle of refraction becomes 90 degrees, and the refracted ray travels along the interface between the two media.

Beyond this critical angle, the light is no longer refracted but is instead reflected back into the denser medium. This is total internal reflection.

The World Chess Federation (FIDE) divides time controls for chess into "classical" time controls, and the fast chess time controls.

Fast chess is subdivided, by decreasing time controls, into rapid chess, blitz chess, and bullet chess.

Time controls for each player in a game of rapid chess are, according to FIDE, more than 10 minutes but less than 60 minutes.

Time controls for each player in a game of blitz chess are, according to FIDE, 10 minutes or less per player.

Bullet chess games have less than three minutes per player, based on a 40-move game;some chess servers rate one-minute-per-player games separately.

Lower time controls are called "hyperbullet" and "ultrabullet" for 30-second-per-player and 15-second-per-player games, respectively.

questions.question: In the following question, one of the parts of the sentence may have error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If the sentence is free from error, select answer option accordingly. Both Monika as well as Raechel 1)/ couldn't state what Chandler's job was 2)/ and lost the bet to Joey and Chandler. 3)/ No error 4)
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, one of the parts of the sentence may have error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If the sentence is free from error, select answer option accordingly.

Both Monika as well as Raechel 1)/ couldn't state what Chandler's job was 2)/ and lost the bet to Joey and Chandler. 3)/ No error 4)
questions.solution:
"Both..and" is a correlative conjunction.

"Both..as well as" are grammatically incorrect because "Both..and" are used together.

In the question, "as well as" is used with "Both". Thus, "and" will replace "as well as" in part 1) of the sentence.

Thus, the correct answer is: (a) 1.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence should be: Both Monika and Raechel couldn't state what Chandler's job was and lost the bet to Joey and Chandler.

Additional Information:

Correlative conjunctions are sort of like tag-team conjunctions. They come in pairs, and you have to use both of them in different places in a sentence to make them work. They get their name from the fact that they work together (co-) and relate one sentence element to another. Correlative conjunctions include pairs as given in the table below:

Either...or
Neither...nor
Hardly...when
Scarcely...when
Both..and
If..then
Not only...but also
Rather...than
Whether..or
No sooner..than

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. When the officer caught the clerk taking a bribe, the latter was down on his knees and promised that he wouldn't do these kind of act.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

When the officer caught the clerk taking a bribe, the latter was down on his knees and promised that he wouldn't do these kind of act.
questions.solution:
Don't use 'these' and 'those' with singular nouns like:

Kind
Type
Sort

Instead use, example: I will not do this kind of act.

In the question, "these" precedes "kind", which is grammatically incorrect. Thus, "this" should replace "these" in the sentence.

Thus, the error is in option (b) - these kind of act.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: When the officer caught the clerk taking a bribe, the latter was down on his knees and promised that he wouldn't do this kind of act.

Additional Information:

Generally speaking, we use this/these to refer to people and things, situations and experiences that are close to the speaker or very close in time. We use that/those to refer to people and things, situations and experiences that are more distant, either in time or physically.

questions.question: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. The new batch of students, along with their instructor, (are planning a trip) soon.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.

The new batch of students, along with their instructor, (are planning a trip) soon.
questions.solution:
The error in the bracketed segment "are planning a trip" is related to subject-verb agreement. The main subject of the sentence is "The new batch of students." Phrases like "along with," "together with," "as well as," etc., that introduce an additional noun do not change the number of the subject. "Batch" is a singular collective noun, and in this context, it acts as a single unit. Therefore, it requires a singular verb.

a) "is planning a trip" - This option correctly uses the singular verb "is" (to agree with the singular subject "batch") and maintains the present continuous tense appropriate for a future plan.

b) "are plan a trip" - The verb "are" is plural and incorrect. Also, "plan" is the base form and doesn't fit the continuous tense.

c) "were planning a trip" - The verb "were" is plural and incorrect. Also, this changes the tense to past continuous, which might not be intended if the planning is current or for the future.

d) "is planned a trip" - This structure is passive ("is planned") and is not meaningful here. "A trip is planned" would be passive, but "batch is planned a trip" is incorrect. Since the focus of the sentence is on the doer "the new batch of students", the active voice construction fits better here.

The correct sentence is: The new batch of students, along with their instructor, is planning a trip soon.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is option a).

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Collective Noun: It is the name given to a number (or collection) of persons or things taken together and spoken of as one whole. Examples could be crowd, fleet, committee, family, army, jury, heard, etc.

Voice of a sentence - Depending upon the emphasis we want to lay we use a particular voice in a particular context. We use active voice to lay emphasis on the doer of the action while we use passive voice to lay emphasis on the receiver of the action.

Example:

Active- Radha will work. (emphasis on Radha)

Passive- Work will be done by Radha. (emphasis on Work)

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb ['was'] and the preposition "by" is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice is an interrogative sentence in Past Indefinite tense, so the Active voice begins with "Did."

In Passive voice, the format is: Was/Were + Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Therefore, the format of the sentence which begins with "Did" in Active voice is: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

For example:

Were you beaten by him? (Passive)

Did he beat you? (Active)

Only option a) matches the structure.

Correct answer: a) Did the linguists translate the historical manuscript last year?

Note: V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

NOTE:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Simple Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object).

For example:

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

· The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

· The verb 'promised' (past simple) is changed into 'had promised' (past perfect).

· 'Here' is changed into 'there'.

· The pronoun 'you' is changed into 'me'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: The officer told me that she had promised to meet me there at 5 pm.

questions.question: The sentence "By maintaining low temperatures, these systems slow down the growth of bacteria and reduce spoilage" is an example of:
questions.questionHtml: The sentence "By maintaining low temperatures, these systems slow down the growth of bacteria and reduce spoilage" is an example of:
questions.solution:
The sentence "By maintaining low temperatures, these systems slow down the growth of bacteria and reduce spoilage" demonstrates a cause-and-effect relationship. The action of maintaining low temperatures is the cause, and the resulting slower bacterial growth and reduced spoilage is the effect.

• Chronological sequence - Incorrect, because the sentence does not describe events in a time order.

• Comparison and contrast - Incorrect, as there is no comparison between two items or ideas.

• Problem and solution - Incorrect, because the sentence explains a natural effect of an action, not a solution to a problem.

This explanation is supported in the first paragraph of the passage, where the author explains how cold storage preserves food.

questions.solution:
The passage begins by introducing cold storage technology and explaining its role in preserving food and ensuring supply. It then discusses concerns associated with prolonged storage, including the survival of harmful bacteria, loss of nutritional value, and the health risks of processed foods. Finally, the passage concludes with a balanced recommendation, emphasizing that while cold storage is valuable, proper handling and consumption practices are necessary to minimize health risks. This pattern of presenting advantages, then concerns, and ending with a balanced conclusion is evident throughout the first, second, and third paragraphs of the passage. Therefore, option (b) accurately describes the structure.

Option (a) Incorrect: There is no historical background or future prediction presented.

Option (c) Incorrect: The passage does not compare cold storage with agricultural practices.

Option (d) Incorrect: The discussion is broader than bacterial growth and does not cover global nutrition policies.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.solution:
The author's attitude toward cold storage technology is balanced and cautious. Throughout the passage, the author acknowledges the benefits of cold storage, such as reducing food wastage, preserving perishable items, and ensuring food availability. At the same time, the passage highlights potential risks, including the survival of harmful bacteria, loss of nutritional value, and health concerns from processed foods. The author does not fully criticize or blindly support cold storage but recommends proper handling and informed consumption to maximize benefits while minimizing risks. This careful evaluation is evident across all three paragraphs of the passage, where advantages, concerns, and recommendations are discussed. Therefore, option (d) accurately reflects the author's attitude.

Option (a) Strongly critical - Incorrect, because the author also emphasizes clear benefits.

Option (b) Neutral and purely descriptive - Incorrect, as the passage evaluates both pros and cons rather than merely describing.

Option (c) Completely supportive - Incorrect, since potential risks and health concerns are clearly noted.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the sentence from the passage which is in the passive voice.

options.text: Cold storage facilities help preserve fruits, vegetables, dairy products, and meat for longer periods.
options.html: Cold storage facilities help preserve fruits, vegetables, dairy products, and meat for longer periods.

options.text: Fresh fruits and vegetables gradually lose vitamins and minerals during prolonged refrigeration.
options.html: Fresh fruits and vegetables gradually lose vitamins and minerals during prolonged refrigeration.

options.text: Regular consumption of such foods has been associated with lifestyle diseases such as obesity, hypertension, and diabetes.
options.html: Regular consumption of such foods has been associated with lifestyle diseases such as obesity, hypertension, and diabetes.

options.text: Cold storage encourages the large-scale storage of processed and packaged foods.
options.html: Cold storage encourages the large-scale storage of processed and packaged foods.

questions.solution:
The sentence "Regular consumption of such foods has been associated with lifestyle diseases such as obesity, hypertension, and diabetes" is in the passive voice. In passive constructions, the subject receives the action rather than performing it. Here, "Regular consumption of such foods" is the subject that receives the action of being associated with diseases, while the doer (researchers or studies) is not explicitly mentioned.

Explanation of other options in brief:

• (a) Cold storage facilities help preserve.. - Active voice; the subject "Cold storage facilities" performs the action.

• (b) Fresh fruits and vegetables gradually lose.. - Active voice; the subject performs the action.

• (d) Cold storage encourages.. - Active voice; the subject performs the action.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

In the sentence "food can be transported over long distances and stored for extended durations without immediate deterioration," the word deterioration refers to food gradually becoming worse in quality, freshness, or safety over time.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. her shoulders in response, wishing P. feeling overwhelmed by the endless Q. choices, she could only shrug R. for a moment of clarity amid S. the chaotic whirlwind of options
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

O. her shoulders in response, wishing

P. feeling overwhelmed by the endless

Q. choices, she could only shrug

R. for a moment of clarity amid

S. the chaotic whirlwind of options
questions.solution:
After reading all the parts thoroughly, we can say that pairing P with Q logically presents the cause of overwhelming feeling (endless choices) and her reaction (shrugging). Next pairing O and R conveys that she hopes for clarity in the midst of her confusion. Finally, S describes the disorienting environment that fuels her wish for clarity, providing context to her overwhelmed state. Therefore, the correct order is PQORS. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The final sentence: Feeling overwhelmed by the endless choices, she could only shrug her shoulders in response, wishing for a moment of clarity amid the chaotic whirlwind of options.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The UN accomplishes this by working to prevent conflict, helping parties in conflict, deploying peacekeepers. B. These activities often overlap and should reinforce one another, to be effective. C. The United Nations (UN) was created in 1945, following the devastation of the Second World War. D. The central mission of the UN is the maintenance of international peace and security.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. The UN accomplishes this by working to prevent conflict, helping parties in conflict, deploying peacekeepers.

B. These activities often overlap and should reinforce one another, to be effective.

C. The United Nations (UN) was created in 1945, following the devastation of the Second World War.

D. The central mission of the UN is the maintenance of international peace and security.
questions.solution:
Sentence C comes first as it introduces us to the main subject of the passage 'The United Nations (UN)'. Sentence D talks about the central mission of the UN. A follows D as it talks about the activities of the UN to accomplish peace and security. 'This' in A refers to the central mission of UN as mentioned in D. B follows A as it builds up on sentence A. 'These activities' in B refers to conflict prevention, and peacekeeping, as mentioned in A.

Therefore, CDAB becomes the correct order among the given options. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: A Pyrrhic victory
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the correct meaning of the idiom:

A Pyrrhic victory

options.text: A triumph gained through collaborative effort
options.html: A triumph gained through collaborative effort

options.text: A win achieved at such a great cost that it is practically a loss
options.html: A win achieved at such a great cost that it is practically a loss

options.text: A success that leads to unexpected fame
options.html: A success that leads to unexpected fame

options.text: A goal accomplished earlier than expected
options.html: A goal accomplished earlier than expected

questions.solution:
"A Pyrrhic victory" refers to a victory so costly that any sense of success is negated by the losses incurred.

Option (b) conveys this paradoxical outcome.

Options (a), (c), and (d) present positive or straightforward successes and thus fail to capture the self-defeating nature of the idiom.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
